newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher on warrant opening.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher on warrant opening.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Tuesday for a fourth straight session as investors bought up stocks newly certified as eligible for inclusion in Taiwan's debut warrants, especially those in electronics, brokers said.
The benchmark index ended 58.48 points or 0.71 percent at 8,255.78, breaking through technical resistance at 8,250.
Turnover was moderately active at T$117.6 billion.
Most warrant-eligible shares, especially electronics, rose on hopes that issuers or investors would buy such shares to build up positions before future warrant issues, brokers said.
"Among warrant-eligible shares, electronics, which have the best profit outlook, naturally attract the heaviest buying," said Michael Hung, an independent analyst.
Electronics rose 2.09 percent, with computer maker Compal Electronics up T$4.5 to T$105, computer peripheral maker Acer Peripherals surging T$5 to T$86, and computer giant Acer up T$1 to T$83.
Leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor, though not a warrant-eligible share, surged T$5.5 to T$124.5 on expected sound outlook in coming quarters.
China-concept shares, or firms with investment or investment plans in mainland China, continued to rise, but their gains had slowed, with Chen Shin Rubber up T$1.1 to T$48.4.
China-concepts have been strong recently, boosted by gains in kindred China-related shares in the Hong Kong market ahead of the British colony's July 1 handover to Beijing, brokers said.
